source_context: The .009 assembly draws a vertical C74 body in the narrow gap between horizontal D25 and D23, with lead strokes above and below the package row. Sheet-1 groups C74 with the +5 V-to-ground C74-C78 bypasses.

decision: The distinct front gap annulus near (1012,1255) matches the separate solder upper-strip spur near (2705,1390), a photo-supported +5 V-side search feature. The lower front hole near (1005,1517) matches the drilled end of a lower broad-strip spur near solder (2705,1647), supported by the same x fit and about 130-pixel front-to-solder row offset; that strip is shared with D23/D25 ground contacts. A second front lower feature near (1005,1465) projects to the same spur at y about 1595, where bright copper obscures any drill. Thus a ground-side search site is localized, but which of the two lower front features is C74's actual lower pad remains open. The .009 assembly outline is not to scale and no capacitor body bridges the D25/D23 gap, so C74 refdes, exact pad pair and owner population remain unproved.
contact_identity_check: The U-shaped copper meets D25's rightmost upper contact in the owner photo. On the current source PCB, D25 is a 20-pin footprint with its rightmost upper contact numbered 11 and named D25_T, while D25.20 is +5 V and D25.9/.10 are ground. This package-position match makes the loop a signal-contact feature in the replica model, not a supported +5 V/GND C74 landing. The owner's contact-to-net identity still needs continuity; do not promote the model net to measured owner copper.
front_seam_anchor_correction: Native front crop (880,1180)-(1120,1380) distinguishes the drilled annulus near (1012,1255) at the D23 molded-notch edge from D23's actual first upper package contact around x1060. The earlier use of x1008 as D23.20 was a feature-identification error. D25.11's upper contact is around x955. A native solder coordinate grid then corrects the earlier, two-pitch-shifted solder assignment: D25.11 is near x2755, the gap spur near x2705 and D23.20 near x2655, all on the upper row y about 1390. The corrected local reflected x scale is roughly -0.95 px/px across the 105-pixel front package seam.
upper_gap_spur_cross_face_check: With D25.11 front x955/solder x2755 and D23.20 front x1060/solder x2655, a linear seam fit predicts front gap annulus x1012 at solder x2701; the observed independent upper broad-strip spur is near (2705,1390), about 4 px away in x and at the corresponding upper-contact row. The front image clearly shows an annulus at about (1012,1255), not a package contact. This is strong same-hole geometric evidence that the gap annulus joins the upper strip, whose D23.20 contact is source-assigned +5 V. It remains a C74 candidate rather than a numbered capacitor pad without a proved lower mate or owner population.
upper_annulus_cross_face_check: The separate front open annuli near (930,1070) and (987,1130) lie about 130–190 px above the package upper-contact row. The corrected seam x fit puts their first solder search columns around x2780 and x2725 respectively, with substantial vertical and perspective uncertainty. A native solder crop above the broad upper strip shows long narrow traces but no isolated drill that can be assigned to either. Do not confuse those higher annuli with the row-height gap annulus (1012,1255), which matches the upper-strip spur near x2705/y1390.
lower_annulus_front_trace_check: A native front crop (930,1300)-(1070,1570) magnifies the two near-x1005 lower features. The first near y1465 has a soldered/bright centre; the second near y1517 is partly hidden by the EPROM socket edge. Neither has a continuous exposed F.Cu trace to the nearest D23 lower contact in this view. The corrected cross-face seam registration instead places them on the lower broad-strip spur at solder x about 2705, y about 1595 and 1647; the latter is a visibly drilled hole. The bright vertical D23 front departure immediately to their right ends separately.
lower_ground_spur_cross_face_check: The corrected x fit from D25.11 front x955/solder x2755 and D23.20 front x1060/solder x2655 predicts front lower x1005 at solder x2707. Using the upper-contact row and lower package row as y controls gives about +130 px solder-minus-front offset: front y1517 predicts solder y1647, where a distinct open hole lies at x about 2705 and connects by a short vertical B.Cu spur to the shared D23/D25 lower strip. Front y1465 predicts solder y1595 at the upper end of the same spur, but broad bright copper and solder obscure an independent drill there. The rear open hole is therefore a strong geometric counterpart of the lower front hole; the upper lower-front feature remains a possible same-strip plated site, not a separately proved C74 pad. The strip's GND assignment follows D23.10/D25.10 package contact identity, not owner meter continuity.
comparative_bypass_spacing: The exact .009 assembly draws C74 and adjacent C75 with the same vertical body-and-lead symbol. In July owner component tiles, C75's candidate upper D29.20 contact and lower annulus are about 215 px apart at (490,1465)/(490,1680); see c75-c76-photo-review.json. C74's upper gap annulus (1012,1255) to the first lower feature (1005,1465) spans about 210 px, whereas to the second lower hole (1005,1517) it spans about 262 px. Similar photo scale and the repeated assembly symbol make the first lower feature the more plausible intended C74 lower lead by geometry. C75's own lower-pad identity is still provisional, and assembly drawings are not drill templates, so this ranking does not establish a numbered C74 pad. Both lower features appear on or beside the same ground-strip spur; direct continuity and a clearer bare-board/assembly view are needed before choosing one.
may_population_check: Earlier May 19 owner component photo PXL_20260519_201918916.jpg, raw crop (600,1600)-(1150,2250), shows the same D23/D25 seam after image rotation: D23 is above D25 and the narrow gap has exposed board/copper without a capacitor body or visible bridge. The July close-up independently shows the gap bare. This supports owner-board nonpopulation on both dates, not factory DNP status or a choice of which lower hole the .009 assembly intended.
may_seam_feature_check: In a wider native May crop (600,1700)-(1300,2350), a separate round annulus sits to the right of the rotated D23/D25 seam near image (1045,1950), consistent with July's gap annulus near (1012,1255) after the package-row rotation. This independent date and angle supports that the July gap ring is a real board feature rather than a highlight on D23's molded notch. The May view does not uniquely separate the two July lower features on the opposite side of the rotated package row; it does not select the C74 lower pad.
alternate_solder_spur_check: The overlapping preceding solder tile 200509593, native crop (3350,1350)-(4080,2050), shows the same D23/D25 lower broad strip and its downward drilled spur from another camera position. The lower open hole is distinct again; the bright junction at the top of the spur still does not resolve a separate drill for the front feature near y1465. This confirms the first lower feature cannot be promoted to a separate through-hole merely by bright solder in the primary tile. The two views do not settle which lower feature is the intended C74 lead.
lower_solder_pair_check: Native solder crop (2350,1320)-(2850,1850) shows two vertically spaced drilled/soldered sites near (2510,1670) and (2510,1750), each on a different narrow horizontal route below the broad D23/D25 lower strip. Their stacked appearance resembles the two front lower holes. The corrected package-row x fit projects front x1005 near solder x2707, roughly 197 px from those sites, or about four solder pin pitches. Vertical perspective skew and the absence of a same-hole control prevent a categorical exclusion, but the proposed match is strongly weakened. Do not assign these two signal-route sites as C74's ground side without a stronger cross-face registration or continuity.
solder_side_limit: A ten-contact count per package row in tile 200514102 places D23.20 at the upper broad-strip spur near x2655 and D25.11/D25_T at the separately traced upper joint near x2755. The other broad-strip spur near x2705 is an intervening solder site in the D23/D25 gap, not D23.19 or D25.11; a matching front annulus near (1012,1255) supplies a strong same-hole geometric candidate. D23.19 is the prior contact near x2605. The lower-left pairs of D23 and D25 join a common broad strip (see d25-ground-strip-orientation-review.json), and its x2705 drilled spur matches the lower front hole near (1005,1517). The first lower front feature near y1465 projects onto the same spur but has no independently resolved backside drill. No unique numbered C74 pad pair follows from these photos.
next_inspection: Meter front gap annulus (1012,1255) to known +5 V and both lower x1005 features to known ground with power off. Determine which lower hole, if either, was intended for C74 using a clearer assembly or unpopulated-board view before assigning a C74 footprint or owner population.
